dct_description_sm:
Annual Active Transportation Capital Investments | Squamish Community Dashboard

About this indicator:

This measure tracks the District's annual municipal budget line item allocated towards Active Transportation capital projects for walking and cycling infrastructure each year. It includes annual transportation capital investments, as well as grant-funded projects, Development Cost Charge funds, and any contributed assets from Community Amenity Contributions.

Analysis:

In 2022-24 the community invested significantly in Active Transportation projects, with total capital investments and contributions of $1.3M in 2022, $2.8M in 2023, and $850,000 in 2024. Recent project highlights include:

• Protected bike lanes on Mamquam Drive, 

• Corridor Trail extension along Tantalus Road 

• New sidewalk on Perth Drive

• Protected bike lanes on Highlands Way South

• Multi-use pathway and safety upgrades on Garibaldi Way between Highway 99 and Tantalus Road 

• New multi-use pathway to the Sp’akw'us Feather Park

• New mutli-use pathway on Pioneer Way and more.


Previous Work: 

The District's work on Active Transportation in 2021 included:

• Spending considerable time preparing for projects to be completed in 2022/23. 

• Completed a significant project: the Pemberton Avenue bike lanes

• Corridor Trail lighting Project was underway (Finch to Adventure Centre and Mamquam Bridge to Mamquam Road) – the conduit and bases were installed, with the lighting set for completion in 2022. 

• Sidewalk and bike lanes on Mamquam Road west of Highway 99, and on Perth Drive in design stages.


In 2020 the District invested $1.1M in Active Transportation with work including: 

• The Corridor Trail connection at Clarke Drive. 

• The Government Road Multi-Use Path north of Depot.

• An intersection improvement for pedestrians at Government Road/Axen Road.

• An improved connection for the Discovery Trail at Industrial and Hwy 99.

• Road widening on the south side of Finch Drive for a bike lane extension, and 

• The Hunter Place connector trail north of Pemberton Avenue. 


In 2019 the District invested $855,000 in Active Transportation with work including: 

• Discovery Trail improvements (widening and paving a 600m segment).

• Diamond Head Road sidewalk construction (65m)

• 60 metres of path widening and paving at Mamquam Elementary to the highway overpass.

• Shoulder widening at Judd Road (480m), Tantalus Road (90m), and Guilford Drive (215m). 


In 2018 the District invested $700,000 in Active Transportation with work including: 

Completing three Active Transportation projects for improved access to and around District schools: 

• 115 metres of paved pathway on Portree Way to Garibaldi Elementary

• 100 metres of sidewalk along Government Road to Mamquam Elementary;

• 360 metres of paved pathway along Buckley Avenue in front of Howe Sound Secondary School and Ecole Squamish Elementary. 

These infrastructure improvements were prioritized as part of the District's Active and Safe Routes to School program.

Reason for monitoring:

Active forms of transportation increase physical activity and health while reducing greenhouse gas emissions from transportation sources.
